full_text_en:
Chengdu Xunjie Communication Chain Co., Ltd. v. Sichuan Shudu Industrial Co., Ltd. and Sichuan Youli Investment Holding Co., Ltd. — dispute over house sale contract

[Ruling Summary]

I. The fundamental criterion for determining whether a contract entered into between the parties is a principal contract or a preliminary contract shall be the parties' expression of intent, that is, whether the parties intend to enter into a new contract in the future to finally clarify the specific content of a certain legal relationship to be formed between them. With respect to whether a preliminary or principal contract relationship exists between the parties, it shall not be determined solely in isolation based on the terms of the agreement entered into between the parties, but rather a comprehensive examination shall be conducted of the content of the relevant agreement as well as facts such as the negotiations subsequently conducted by the parties to reach a transaction and the relevant performance conduct, so as to ascertain the true intent of the parties and thereby accurately define the nature of the legal relationship between the parties.

II. In accordance with the spirit of Article 15 of the Property Law of the PRC, a disposing act is distinct from a binding act, and rescission of a contract is not a means of disposing of property. Whether a contract is rescinded does not involve a change in ownership of the property, but only relates to whether the parties continue to bear the obligations agreed upon in the contract.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2013) Min Ti Zi No. 90

Applicant for retrial (plaintiff at first instance, counterclaim defendant, appellee at second instance): Chengdu Xunjie Communication Chain Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 155 Tai Sheng South Road, Chengdu, Sichuan Province.

Legal representative: Wang Aidong, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Wei, lawyer of Beijing Tian Tong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Chen Yaoquan, lawyer of Beijing Tian Tong Law Firm.

Applicant for retrial (defendant at first instance, counterclaim plaintiff, appellant at second instance): Sichuan Shudu Industrial Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 20 Shu Wa Bei San Street, Chengdu, Sichuan Province.

Legal representative: Cheng Gaochao, Chairman of the board of directors of the company.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Xueping, lawyer of Beijing Dishi Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Shi Han, lawyer of Sichuan Jingji Law Firm.

Third party at first instance: Sichuan Youli Investment Holding Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 20 Shu Wa Bei San Street, Shudu Avenue, Chengdu, Sichuan Province.

Legal representative: Li Fenglin, Chairman of the board of directors of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Gu, lawyer of Sichuan Jingji Law Firm.

With respect to the dispute over a house sale contract between the applicant for retrial Chengdu Xunjie Communication Chain Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xunjie Company) and Sichuan Shudu Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shudu Industrial Company) and the third party at first instance Sichuan Youli Investment Holding Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Youli Company), the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province rendered the Civil Judgment (2010) Cheng Min Chu Zi No. 433 on January 20, 2011. Shudu Industrial Company, being dissatisfied with the judgment, filed an appeal to the Sichuan High People's Court. The said court rendered the Civil Ruling (2011) Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 247 on July 25, 2011, ruling to set aside the original judgment and remand the case to the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province for retrial. The Chengdu Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province rendered the Civil Judgment (2011) Cheng Min Chu Zi No. 936 on December 29, 2011. Shudu Industrial Company, being dissatisfied with the judgment, filed an appeal to the Sichuan High People's Court, which rendered the Civil Judgment (2012) Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 331 on December 2, 2012. Xunjie Company, being dissatisfied with the judgment, filed an application for retrial with this Court. This Court rendered the Civil Ruling (2013) Min Shen Zi No. 188 on April 3, 2013, granting the retrial of this case, and during the retrial, the execution of the original judgment was suspended. After granting the retrial of this case, this Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a hearing in this case on June 21, 2013. The agents ad litem of Xunjie Company, Zheng Wei and Chen Yaoquan, the agents ad litem of Shudu Industrial Company, Jiang Xueping and Shi Han, and the agent ad litem of Youli Company, Zhao Gu, attended the proceedings. Before the hearing, Shudu Industrial Company submitted a counterclaim for retrial to this Court, and this Court listed it as an applicant for retrial in accordance with law. The trial of this case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found through trial:

(1) On September 20, 2006, Shudu Industrial Company (Party A) and Xunjie Company (Party B) entered into the "Agreement on the Purchase of House Property" stipulating: "Parties A and B, in accordance with the principles of mutual benefit and mutual advantage, after multiple consultations, have reached the following consensus regarding the sale of the north first floor and atrium of Shudu Building: 1. Party B purchases the building area of 2,100 square meters of the north first floor and atrium of Shudu Building owned by Party A, at a total price of RMB 67,500,000 (final settlement shall be made based on the property ownership certificate issued by the housing authority). 2. From the date of signing this agreement, upon receipt by Party A of a deposit of RMB 10,000,000 for the intended purchase paid by Party B, the said deposit shall automatically be converted into the purchase payment when the purchase contract is signed. 3. Parties A and B shall conduct specific consultations on issues such as the purchase contract and payment method under the principles of this agreement. 4. Both Parties A and B shall abide by the principles established in this agreement; breach shall cause the breaching party to pay liquidated damages of RMB 10,000,000 to the non-breaching party. 5. This agreement shall automatically become invalid upon the signing of the house sale contract between the parties."

The above facts are confirmed by the "Agreement on the Purchase of House Property" bearing the official seals of Xunjie Company and Shudu Industrial Company. The parties have no objection to the authenticity of the said evidence, and the court of first instance confirmed it.

(2) On September 14, 2006, and September 18, 2006, Xunjie Company transferred RMB 2,000,000 and RMB 3,000,000 respectively through the Chengdu Branch of Shanghai Pudong Development Bank Co., Ltd. to the account of Sichuan Shuka Special Fiber Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shuka Fiber Company, now named Youli Company) at the Chengdu Branch of China Everbright Bank, with the purpose of the payment being a deposit for the intended purchase of the house property. On September 18, 2006, September 19, 2006, and September 20, 2006, Xunjie Company transferred RMB 2,000,000, RMB 2,000,000, and RMB 1,000,000 respectively through the Chengdu Branch of China Everbright Bank to the account of Shuka Fiber Company. On September 20, 2006, Shuka Fiber Company issued two receipts for deposit amounts of RMB 5,000,000 each to Xunjie Company. On January 4, 2007, Shudu Industrial Company delivered the disputed house property to Xunjie Company for use, and it has been used by Xunjie Company up to the present.

The above facts are confirmed by the "Credit Voucher of China Everbright Bank for Inter-Bank Accounts", "Electronic Transfer Voucher of Shanghai Pudong Development Bank", "Sichuan Province Non-Operational Settlement Unified Invoice" issued by Shuka Fiber Company, and the consistent statements of Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company regarding the time of delivery of the house property.

(3) The Sichuan Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce approved the change of the enterprise name from "Chengdu Shudu Building Co., Ltd." to "Sichuan Shuka Special Fiber Co., Ltd." in 2004. Sichuan Shudu Building Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shudu Building Company) was established with capital contributions of RMB 46,000,000 (46%), RMB 5,000,000 (5%), and RMB 49,000,000 (49%) from Shuka Fiber Company, Chengdu Shudu Investment Management Co., Ltd., and Jiangsu Shuangliang Technology Co., Ltd. respectively. On July 2005, Shudu Building Company was divided into Shudu Building Company and Shudu Industrial Company. The registered capital of Shudu Industrial Company is RMB 10,000,000, and the names and contribution ratios of the shareholders remained unchanged. On April 10, 2009, the Sichuan Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce approved the change of the enterprise name of Shuka Fiber Company to Youli Company.

The above facts are confirmed by the business registration materials including the "Notice of Approval for Change of Enterprise Name", "Company Change Registration Application", "Business License", "Company Articles of Association", and "Shudu Building Division Agreement" (all copies with the special seal for enterprise registration of the Chengdu Administration for Industry and Commerce).

(4) On August 5, 2005, the "Site Certificate" issued by Shudu Building Company stated: "Due to the division of the enterprise, the south building (Quan 0111476), north building (Quan 0963909), atrium (Quan 0111478) from the first to fourth floors, and the boutique (Quan 0613360) of Shudu Building located at No. 20 Shu Wa Bei San Street, Jinjiang District, under the name of Shudu Building Company, are provided free of charge to Shudu Industrial Company for use." On February 25, 2006, Shudu Building Company and Shudu Industrial Company, based on the division agreement signed by both parties, entered into an "Agreement on Handling the Transfer and Registration of Ownership of the First to Fourth Floors of Shudu Building Podium" regarding the specific issues of transferring and registering the ownership of the house property and corresponding land use rights of 17,537.36 square meters of the podium of Shudu Building (including south building, north building, and atrium) located at No. 20 Shu Wa Bei San Street, Jinjiang District, Chengdu, from the first to fourth floors and the boutique, to the name of Shudu Industrial Company. Both parties agreed to handle the transfer and registration procedures for the property ownership that should be transferred and registered to Shudu Industrial Company in installments, and each party appointed one person to jointly handle the transfer and registration procedures for the property ownership. The relevant costs were to be borne by the parties respectively in accordance with regulations. After all the said house properties were transferred and registered under the name of Shudu Industrial Company, the transfer and registration procedures for the corresponding land use rights certificates were to be commenced immediately. On March 4, 2008, the Chengdu Real Estate Title Supervision Office issued to Shudu Industrial Company the property ownership certificate (Certificate No.: Cheng Fang Quan Jian Zheng Zi No. 1654684, Hill (Plot) No.: Quan 1223775) for the first floor, area 4,060.40 square meters, located at No. 20 Shu Wa Bei San Street, Jinjiang District, Chengdu. On March 14, 2008, Youli Company borrowed RMB 30,000,000 from the Chengdu Shudu Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd., and Shudu Industrial Company provided a mortgage guarantee for Youli Company's borrowing with 2,043.91 square meters of the house property under the said certificate, and registered the mortgage with the Real Estate Title Supervision Office of Chengdu Real Estate Administration Bureau. Youli Company repaid all the principal and interest of the loan to the Chengdu Shudu Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd. on December 15, 2009, but the mortgage registration has not been cancelled. On July 29, 2010, Shudu Industrial Company set a mortgage for Youli Company's comprehensive credit facility of RMB 25,000,000 with the Chengdu Shuncheng Street Sub-branch of China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd. using 1,347.52 square meters of the house property located at No. 20 Shu Wa Bei San Street, Jinjiang District, Chengdu (Certificate No.: Cheng Fang Quan Jian Zheng Zi No. 1654684), and registered the mortgage with the Real Estate Title Supervision Office of Chengdu Real Estate Administration Bureau. Youli Company borrowed RMB 5,000,000 under the credit facility and repaid the principal and interest on November 19, 2010, but the mortgage registration has not been cancelled.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the "Site Certificate" issued by Shudu Building Company on August 5, 2005, the "Agreement on Handling the Transfer and Registration of Ownership of the First to Fourth Floors of Shudu Building Podium" signed by Shudu Building Company and Shudu Industrial Company on February 25, 2006, the "House Ownership Certificate", the "House Information Summary" issued by Chengdu Real Estate Archives Bureau, and the "Situation Explanations" respectively issued by the Chengdu Shudu Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd. and the Chengdu Shuncheng Street Sub-branch of China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd.

(5) On September 28, 2009, Xunjie Company sent a "Commercial Letter" to Shudu Industrial Company, the main content being: "The erosion of the industry by the financial crisis and changes in the market have caused a sharp decline in our company's mobile phone sales and profits; on the other hand, the overall downward trend in real estate sales prices, could your company make certain concessions on the agreed purchase price based on the original agreement? Our expectation is around RMB 60,000,000." On September 28, 2009, Shudu Industrial Company sent a letter to Xunjie Company, requesting Xunjie Company to arrange personnel to negotiate with Shudu Industrial Company regarding the formal house sale contract within 30 days and pay the site use fee for three years. The next day, Xunjie Company replied, agreeing to discuss the house purchase matters on October 9, 2009. On October 10, 2009, Shudu Industrial Company sent a letter to Xunjie Company, requesting a reply to the draft "House Sale Contract" prepared by Shudu Industrial Company. Xunjie Company replied on October 12, 2009, confirming receipt of the draft "House Sale Contract" provided by Shudu Industrial Company. On October 20, 2009, October 28, 2009, and December 9, 2009, Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company organized relevant personnel and lawyers to conduct three negotiations on relevant issues concerning the house sale. The parties failed to reach an agreement after negotiating issues such as whether Xunjie Company should pay a site use fee, the burden of transaction and transfer taxes and fees, the handling of the property ownership certificate and the payment time of the balance of the purchase price, and the release of the mortgage on the sold house property. On November 4, 2009, Shudu Industrial Company sent a letter to Xunjie Company, requesting Xunjie Company to pay a site use fee, with the specific standard to be negotiated by the parties, and that all taxes and fees for the house sale be borne entirely by Xunjie Company. The next day, Xunjie Company replied, disagreeing to pay the site use fee, requesting that the burden of taxes and fees be borne separately by Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company for their respective parts in accordance with national laws, regulations, and policies, and Xunjie Company agreed to pay all remaining purchase price immediately after the transfer and registration of the house property and land use rights. On November 12, 2009, Shudu Industrial Company sent a letter to Xunjie Company, the main content being: 1. The parties had been negotiating the content of a house sale contract based on the "Agreement on the Purchase of House Property" for three years, but serious differences still existed on many major issues of the sale contract, resulting in the parties not signing a "House Sale Contract", therefore the house sale relationship between the parties was not established. 2. Xunjie Company had occupied Shudu Industrial Company's house property for three years without compensation and should pay a site occupancy use fee. 3. Shudu Industrial Company disagreed with the payment method proposed by Xunjie Company. 4. It was Shudu Industrial Company's transaction condition for selling second-hand houses that Xunjie Company bear all taxes and fees for the house sale, and this had never changed. On November 17, 2009, Xunjie Company replied to Shudu Industrial Company, the main content being: 1. Xunjie Company believed that the house sale between the parties had actually been performed. 2. Xunjie Company's possession and use of the house property were lawful and it should not pay a site occupancy use fee to Shudu Industrial Company. 3. Xunjie Company insisted on paying all the balance of the purchase price to Shudu Industrial Company only after the transfer and registration of the house property. 4. The request by Shudu Industrial Company that all taxes and fees for the house sale be borne entirely by Xunjie Company lacked a basis and violated relevant national laws and regulations. On March 3, 2010, Shudu Industrial Company sent a letter to Xunjie Company through Chengdu Shudu Notary Public Office, the content being: "On December 9, 2009, our parties negotiated relevant follow-up matters, but due to major differences between the parties, no agreement was reached. Subsequently, the parties conducted several negotiations on the follow-up matters, but still achieved no results. For this reason, after careful study, our company hereby notifies your company: 1. The 'Agreement on the Purchase of House Property' signed by our parties on September 20, 2006, is rescinded; 2. Please vacate the said house property within thirty days after receiving this letter; 3. Please pay our company the site use fee payable during the period of occupying the said house property and handle the corresponding financial settlement (refund and payment of fees such as the deposit and use fees) within thirty days after receiving this letter."

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the correspondence exchanged between Xunjie Company and Shudu Industrial Company, the "Meeting Minutes", and the notarized instrument.

Xunjie Company alleged in its complaint at first instance: On September 20, 2006, Xunjie Company and Shudu Industrial Company reached an agreement on the sale and purchase of a house property with a construction area of 2,100 square meters located on the north first floor and atrium of Shudu Building, and signed the "Agreement on the Purchase of House Property", which clearly stipulated the location, area, price, and liability for breach of contract of the said house property. After Xunjie Company paid a deposit of RMB 10,000,000 to Shudu Industrial Company in accordance with the agreement, Shudu Industrial Company delivered the disputed house property to Xunjie Company for use up to the present. The parties orally agreed that after Shudu Industrial Company transferred the house property into Xunjie Company's name, Xunjie Company would pay the remaining purchase price to Shudu Industrial Company promptly. Thereafter, Xunjie Company and Shudu Industrial Company conducted multiple consultations on matters such as the transfer and registration of the house property and the payment of the price but failed to reach an agreement. On March 3, 2010, Shudu Industrial Company served on Xunjie Company a notice letter rescinding the "Agreement on the Purchase of House Property" signed by the parties on September 20, 2006. Xunjie Company believed that the "Agreement on the Purchase of House Property" signed between the parties already met the requirements of Article 5 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Commodity House Sale Contracts, and that after signing the "Agreement on the Purchase of House Property" and after Xunjie Company paid the deposit, Shudu Industrial Company had delivered the house property to Xunjie Company for possession and use, so the parties' "Agreement on the Purchase of House Property" had actually been performed and should be protected by law. Therefore, Xunjie Company requested the court to: 1. Confirm that the "Agreement on the Purchase of House Property" signed by Xunjie Company and Shudu Industrial Company on September 20, 2006, was established and legally valid, and confirm that the rescission notice made by Shudu Industrial Company on March 3, 2010, rescinding the "Agreement on the Purchase of House Property" signed on September 20, 2006, was invalid; 2. Order Shudu Industrial Company to perform its obligation to handle the transfer and registration of the house property ownership to Xunjie Company within 15 days after the judgment takes effect, and within 5 days after Shudu Industrial Company performs the transfer and registration, Xunjie Company shall pay the remaining purchase price of RMB 57,500,000 to Shudu Industrial Company; 3. The taxes and fees for the transfer of ownership shall be borne respectively by Xunjie Company and Shudu Industrial Company in accordance with the law.

Shudu Industrial Company responded in its defense: 1. The "Clarification of Claims" submitted by Xunjie Company to the court is invalid, and the court should not hear its claim for "confirmation that the rescission letter is invalid." 2. At the time of signing the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" on September 20, 2006, Shudu Industrial Company was not yet the owner of the premises; therefore, the agreement is not a contract for the sale of premises. In fact, the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" is an exclusive deposit contract. Xunjie Company also did not pay Shudu Industrial Company a deposit of RMB 10 million, so the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" was established but not yet effective, and has no legal force. During the negotiation process after the agreement was signed, the parties did not discuss matters such as payment of the purchase price or the procedures for the transfer of the premises and the land property rights. Due to reasons not attributable to either party, the contract for the sale of premises has not been signed to date, and neither party bears responsibility for the failure to sign the purchase contract. 3. Using the fact that Xunjie Company is currently using the premises to infer that Shudu Industrial Company has fulfilled its obligation to deliver the premises is a logical error. On January 4, 2007, Shudu Industrial Company allowed Xunjie Company to use the premises because the lease for the premises with a third party expired on December 31, 2006, and allowing Xunjie Company to use them would not affect the negotiations for sale or lease. Therefore, Shudu Industrial Company did not deliver the premises based on a sales relationship. 4. In the three years following the signing of the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises," the parties did not reach a consensus on the sale of the premises. They failed to agree on major transactional terms. The transaction amount for the premises was RMB 67.5 million, while the tax liability was as high as RMB 44.21 million, accounting for 65.51% of the transaction value. Therefore, it is unfair to use the "gap-filling" method provided for in Article 62 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Contract Law") and its judicial interpretations to resolve the significant differences on the transactional terms between the two parties. 5. Even if the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" is a contract for the purchase of premises, and Xunjie Company has paid the deposit and taken possession of the premises based on Shudu Industrial Company's fulfillment of its sale obligations, Shudu Industrial Company lawfully rescinded the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" on March 3, 2010. The agreement was rescinded from the date the rescission letter reached Xunjie Company, i.e., March 8, 2010. Shudu Industrial Company's claim for rescission of the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" under Articles 3, 4, and 94 of the Contract Law and Article 115 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Security Law Interpretation") has sufficient legal basis. On the other hand, Xunjie Company's claims lack contractual basis and contradict the parties' expression of intent. They should all be rejected.

Youli Company did not submit a defense.

Shudu Industrial Company filed a counterclaim at first instance, alleging: Xunjie Company and Shudu Industrial Company signed the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" involved in the case, which stipulated that after Xunjie Company paid the deposit, the two parties should negotiate the main terms of the contract for the sale of premises. After the contract for the sale of premises was signed, the deposit would be converted into the purchase price for the premises, and the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" would automatically become effective. On December 31, 2006, the lease for the premises with a third party expired. At that time, although the parties had not yet reached an agreement on the sale of the premises, based on trust in mutual cooperation and the potential sale, Shudu Industrial Company agreed to allow Xunjie Company to use the premises. After the signing of the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises," during the more than three years from Xunjie Company's actual possession and use of the premises on January 4, 2007, the parties conducted multiple negotiations on the sale of the premises but were unable to reach an agreement and could not sign a contract for the sale of premises. During this period, Xunjie Company possessed and used Shudu Industrial Company's premises for commercial activities and obtained commercial benefits, while the parties were unable to complete the transaction for a long time. As a result, Shudu Industrial Company could neither sell the premises to collect the purchase price nor collect fees for the use of the premises, objectively suffering substantial economic losses. For this reason, on March 3, 2010, Shudu Industrial Company had to send a letter to Xunjie Company, requesting to rescind the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" and demanding that Xunjie Company pay fees for the use of the premises. In summary, the request was: 1. Order Xunjie Company to immediately vacate and return to Shudu Industrial Company the premises located at No. 20, North Third Street, Shudu Avenue, North First Floor and Atrium, with a construction area of approximately 2,100 square meters; 2. Order Xunjie Company to pay Shudu Industrial Company fees for the use of the aforementioned premises from January 4, 2007, until the actual date of vacating (calculated as RMB 26.509 million up to June 30, 2010).

Xunjie Company responded in defense: Xunjie Company's claims are based on the sales relationship between the parties, while Shudu Industrial Company's counterclaim is based on the relationship of possession of the premises. The principal claim and the counterclaim are not based on the same legal relationship and are not adversarial. If the principal claim is established, the counterclaim is not, and vice versa. Therefore, the conditions for Shudu Industrial Company's counterclaim are not met. The counterclaim should not be accepted, or if accepted, the proceedings should be suspended, and it should not be consolidated with the principal claim. Shudu Industrial Company's delivery of the premises was based on the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises." The legal relationship in this case is a sales contract relationship, so Xunjie Company requests confirmation that the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" is established and that both parties should perform their relevant obligations. Furthermore, Shudu Industrial Company's claim for Xunjie Company to pay fees for the use of the premises lacks any legal basis.

Youli Company did not submit a defense.

The court of first instance found: (1) When Xunjie Company filed this lawsuit, the scope of the claims in the complaint included a request to confirm that the rescission letter issued by Shudu Industrial Company on March 3, 2010, rescinding the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" signed by the parties on September 20, 2006, was invalid. Subsequently, Xunjie Company's application to add claims refined and added to the original claims, and did not explicitly waive the claim for a declaration that the rescission letter was invalid. Shudu Industrial Company's argument that Xunjie Company had re-filed its claims and by its actual conduct had waived the disputed claim was not established. Xunjie Company's claims were specific and clear, and the court of first instance confirmed them.

(2) Because Shudu Industrial Company filed a counterclaim based on the rescission of the contract, requesting that Xunjie Company vacate the premises and pay fees for the use of the premises, while Xunjie Company requested specific performance of the contract, it is necessary to determine whether the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" signed by the parties on September 20, 2006, has been rescinded and whether the rescission letter issued by Shudu Industrial Company on March 3, 2010, is valid. Shudu Industrial Company issued a rescission letter on March 3, 2010, rescinding the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" signed by the parties on September 20, 2006. The letter reached Xunjie Company on March 8, 2010. Both parties have no objection to these facts, and the court of first instance confirmed them. A contract may be rescinded by law or by agreement. Article 93 of the Contract Law provides: "The parties may rescind a contract if they reach a consensus through consultation. The parties may agree on the conditions for one party to rescind the contract. When the conditions for rescission are satisfied, the party entitled to rescind may rescind the contract." Article 94 provides for the conditions for statutory rescission. Article 96, paragraph 1, provides: "If a party claims to rescind the contract in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 93 or Article 94, it shall notify the other party. The contract is rescinded when the notice reaches the other party. If the other party objects, it may request a people's court or an arbitration institution to confirm the validity of the rescission." Although Shudu Industrial Company's rescission letter reached Xunjie Company on March 8, 2010, Xunjie Company had already filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance on May 18, 2010, objecting to the validity of the rescission letter. Since the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" did not explicitly provide for the rescission of the contract or the period for raising objections, Xunjie Company's period for raising objections to the validity of the rescission letter does not violate the provisions of Article 24 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (II) (hereinafter referred to as the "Contract Law Interpretation (II)") regarding the period for objections. Shudu Industrial Company now claims, based on Article 94, item (5) of the Contract Law ("other circumstances provided by law") and Article 115 of the Security Law Interpretation, that it exercised its statutory right to rescind because the parties failed to reach an agreement in negotiations. Upon review, this ground does not meet the statutory conditions for rescission of a contract. The rescission letter sent by Shudu Industrial Company is invalid and has no legal effect on Xunjie Company. Therefore, the court of first instance upheld Xunjie Company's claim for a declaration that the rescission letter issued by Shudu Industrial Company on March 3, 2010, rescinding the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" signed on September 20, 2006, was invalid.

(3) Xunjie Company's claims are based on the premise that the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" is a principal contract for the sale of premises and is lawful and valid. Shudu Industrial Company's counterclaim is based on the premise that the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" is a deposit contract for the sale. Contracts are distinguished between preliminary contracts and principal contracts. The purpose of a preliminary contract is to agree to enter into a certain contract in the future when, due to factual or legal obstacles, the main contract cannot be concluded immediately. The obligee under a preliminary contract may only request the other party to perform the obligation to enter into the principal contract, and may not directly request performance according to the terms of the preliminary contract. Article 3 of the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" stipulates that Xunjie Company and Shudu Industrial Company shall conduct specific negotiations on the contract for the purchase of premises and the payment method, among other issues, under the principles of this agreement. Article 5 stipulates that when the parties sign a contract for the sale of the premises, this agreement shall automatically lapse. The content of these provisions indicates that after signing the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises," the parties should further negotiate the sale of the premises and sign a "Contract for the Sale of Premises." However, this does not necessarily mean that the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" is a preliminary contract or a deposit contract, for the following reasons: 1. The "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" contains specific and clear main terms such as the names of the parties, the subject matter, the price, and liability for breach of contract. According to Article 1, paragraph 1 of the Contract Law Interpretation (II), which provides: "If there is a dispute between the parties as to whether a contract is established, and the people's court can determine the names of the parties, the subject matter, and the quantity, the contract shall generally be deemed to be established, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties," the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" should be deemed to have been established because it contains the essential terms of a contract. 2. A deposit for the purchase of premises of RMB 10 million was paid by Xunjie Company to Youli Company, a shareholder of Shudu Industrial Company, before the parties signed the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises." Shudu Industrial Company confirmed in Article 2 of the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" that it had received the aforementioned deposit of RMB 10 million for the purchase of premises paid in advance by Xunjie Company. Therefore, Xunjie Company has fulfilled its contractual obligation to pay the deposit for the purchase of premises. Additionally, although Shudu Industrial Company had not yet obtained ownership of the premises at the time of signing the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises," based on the premises transfer agreement signed by Shudu Industrial Company and Shudu Building Company and the site use certificate issued by Shudu Building Company, it can be proven that Shudu Industrial Company had the right to dispose of the premises in question. Moreover, Shudu Industrial Company has now actually obtained the ownership certificate for the premises in question, and the ownership is clear. This does not have a substantive impact on the establishment and validity of the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises." 3. The provisions of Articles 3 and 5 of the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" require the parties to further negotiate other contents that are missing from the contract and to sign a "Contract for the Sale of Premises," given that the contract already contains the essential terms. According to Article 1, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law Interpretation (II), which provides: "If the parties cannot reach an agreement on other contents of the contract that are missing, which are not covered by the preceding paragraph, the people's court shall determine them in accordance with the relevant provisions of Articles 61, 62, and 125 of the Contract Law," where the parties in this case cannot reach an agreement on other terms, such as the payment method, not covered in the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises," and cannot sign a "Contract for the Sale of Premises," the people's court shall determine them in accordance with the relevant provisions. It cannot be concluded that the contract is not established or that it is a preliminary contract or a deposit contract in nature. 4. After signing the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises," Shudu Industrial Company delivered to Xunjie Company for possession and use the disputed premises located at the North First Floor and Atrium of Shudu Building, with a construction area of 2,100 square meters. Shudu Industrial Company argued that it was negotiating both a sale and a lease with Xunjie Company, and that it delivered the premises to Xunjie Company not based on a sales relationship. Shudu Industrial Company's argument, lacking factual support, cannot be established by law. Xunjie Company's claim that Shudu Industrial Company delivered the premises to it based on a sales relationship is established. Therefore, the court of first instance held that the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" is a contract for the purchase of premises, not a preliminary contract or a deposit contract. It represents the true intention of the parties, its content does not violate relevant legal provisions, and it is lawful and valid. Xunjie Company's request for confirmation that the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" is a contract for the sale of premises that has been established and is lawful and valid is justified and should be upheld.

(4) Regarding Xunjie Company's request for an order that Shudu Industrial Company perform the obligation to assist in the registration procedures for the transfer of the property rights of the premises within 15 days after the judgment becomes effective. Because the parties did not agree on the time for the transfer of the premises in the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises," the court of first instance notified the parties to enter into a supplementary agreement, but they were unable to reach an agreement on this matter. Although registration is the basis for acquiring real property rights, the primary obligation of the seller under a contract for the sale of premises is to deliver the premises to the buyer. The primary obligation of the buyer is to pay the price to the seller. The registration of the transfer is a function of the registration authority. The seller only has the obligation to assist in the registration procedures, which, compared to the obligations to deliver the premises and pay the price, is an ancillary obligation. Since Shudu Industrial Company delivered the premises to Xunjie Company on January 4, 2007, and Xunjie Company has only paid a deposit of RMB 10 million to Shudu Industrial Company, with the balance of the purchase price unpaid, the conditions for Xunjie Company to request Shudu Industrial Company to first assist in the transfer of the premises are not yet ripe, given that the parties have not agreed on the registration of the transfer and Xunjie Company has not paid the majority of the purchase price. After Xunjie Company has fully performed its payment obligation to Shudu Industrial Company, Shudu Industrial Company has an obligation to assist Xunjie Company in the property transfer procedures within a reasonable period. Since relevant administrative regulations and rules do not stipulate the time for registration of the transfer of urban real estate, the court of first instance, by reference to Article 33 of the "Regulations on the Development and Management of Urban Real Estate" promulgated by the State Council, determined that Shudu Industrial Company should assist Xunjie Company in the property transfer procedures within 90 days after receiving the full purchase price.

(5) Regarding Xunjie Company's request for an order that, within 5 days after the transfer of the disputed premises, Xunjie Company pay the remaining purchase price of RMB 57.5 million to Shudu Industrial Company. Because the nature of the legal relationship claimed by Shudu Industrial Company is inconsistent with the nature of the legal relationship determined by the court of first instance, the court of first instance, in accordance with Article 35 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings," explained this to Shudu Industrial Company, but Shudu Industrial Company refused to change its claims. A right of claim means that the obligee may request the obligor to perform or refrain from performing a certain act. For the unpaid purchase price of the premises, Shudu Industrial Company, as the creditor, may file a corresponding claim. However, Xunjie Company, as the obligor, does not have this right of claim. Therefore, the court of first instance did not uphold this claim by Xunjie Company.

(6) Regarding Xunjie Company's request that the tax and fees arising from the registration procedures for the transfer of the property rights of the premises be borne by each party according to law. Because the parties did not agree in the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" on the method of bearing such tax and fees, and the parties could not subsequently reach a supplementary agreement, the tax and fees should be borne by the respective parties in accordance with the relevant national provisions on the burden of tax and fees for the registration of real estate transfers.

(7) Regarding Shudu Industrial Company's counterclaim for an order that Xunjie Company vacate the premises and pay fees for the use of the premises. Because the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" is a contract for the sale of premises, and Shudu Industrial Company delivered the premises to Xunjie Company based on a contractual relationship for the sale of premises, Shudu Industrial Company does not have the right to request Xunjie Company to return the delivered premises while the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" is valid. In addition, since there is no lease relationship between the parties, Shudu Industrial Company does not have the right to demand that Xunjie Company pay fees for the use of the premises. The court of first instance did not uphold Shudu Industrial Company's counterclaim.

In summary, the court of first instance ruled as follows: 1. The "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" signed by Xunjie Company and Shudu Industrial Company on September 20, 2006, is established and valid; 2. The rescission letter issued by Shudu Industrial Company on March 3, 2010, rescinding the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" signed with Xunjie Company on September 20, 2006, is invalid; 3. Within 90 days after Xunjie Company has fully performed its obligation to pay the purchase price to Shudu Industrial Company, Shudu Industrial Company shall assist in the transfer to Xunjie Company of the premises located at No. 20, Shuwa North Third Street, Chengdu, North First Floor and Atrium of Shudu Building, with an area of 2,100 square meters. The tax and fees arising therefrom shall be borne by Xunjie Company and Shudu Industrial Company respectively in accordance with relevant regulations; 4. Reject Xunjie Company's other claims; 5. Reject Shudu Industrial Company's counterclaim. The case acceptance fee for the principal claim was RMB 379,300, and the property preservation fee was RMB 5,000. Xunjie Company shall bear RMB 189,650, and Shudu Industrial Company shall bear RMB 194,650. The case acceptance fee for the counterclaim was RMB 87,172.50, to be borne by Shudu Industrial Company.

Shudu Industrial Company, dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to the High People's Court of Sichuan Province, arguing: 1. The first-instance judgment erroneously found that the deposit contract "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises," which was signed by the parties to enter into the principal contract, is a principal contract for the sale of premises. 2. The first-instance judgment erroneously found that Xunjie Company had delivered the deposit to Shudu Industrial Company. 3. Due to reasons not attributable to either party, a contract of sale was not entered into for over three years. Xunjie Company should vacate the premises and pay usage fees from the date of receipt of the rescission letter. 4. The first-instance procedure was illegal. Xunjie Company had previously waived in writing the claim for a declaration on the validity of the rescission act. In the first instance of the retrial, the court of first instance again had Xunjie Company confirm the claim regarding the validity of the rescission and ruled accordingly. Xunjie Company only raised the claim for a declaration on the validity of the rescission on September 15, 2011, which exceeded the period for objections. Therefore, Shudu Industrial Company requested the setting aside of the first-instance judgment and a ruling in favor of its counterclaim.

Xunjie Company did not submit a written statement of defense but argued orally at the hearing that the first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact, correctly applied the law, and the procedure was lawful, and therefore, Shudu Industrial Company's appeal should be dismissed.

Youli Company did not submit a statement of defense.

The court of second instance found: (1) During the second instance trial, within the evidentiary period designated by the court of second instance, Shudu Industrial Company submitted the following evidence: 1. "Price Assessment Report" (Hong Jia Ping [2011] No. 53), which stated that the assessed rental value of the premises in question from January 1, 2007, to June 30, 2011, was RMB 34,147,200, intended to prove the amount of usage fees. 2. "Tax Consultation Report" issued by Sichuan Qiushi Fiscal and Tax Consulting Co., Ltd. on October 14, 2011, which stated that the tax involved in the transaction of the premises was over RMB 40 million, including land appreciation tax of RMB 32,319,835 payable by the seller according to law, intended to prove that the failure to enter into a contract for the sale of premises within three years was due to a major disagreement that could not be attributed to either party. 3. Four copies of "Contracts for the Sale of Premises" signed by Shudu Industrial Company with other buyers between January 2006 and September 2007, intended to prove that the "Agreement for the Purchase of Premises" is a deposit contract of a preliminary nature.

Xunjie Company stated in its cross-examination that there was no objection to the authenticity of Evidence 1, but it was irrelevant. There was no objection to the authenticity of Evidence 2, which reflected that each party in the real estate sale involved in this case should pay taxes separately, and it conversely proved the existence of a real estate sale relationship between the two parties. There was no objection to the authenticity of Evidence 3, but it was irrelevant.

(2) During the second instance trial, within the time limit for producing evidence designated by the second instance court, Shudu Industrial Company submitted to the court an "Application for Appraisal of Site Occupation and Usage Fees," applying for an appraisal of the site occupation and usage fees for the disputed property from January 4, 2007, to the date of the actual appraisal.

(3) On September 28, 2009, Shudu Industrial Company sent a letter to Xunjie Company, the main content of which was: "Since the signing of the 'Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate' between our two parties on September 20, 2006, three years have passed, but our two parties have still not been able to sign a formal 'Real Estate Sale Contract.' On June 2, 2009, your company sent a 'Business Letter' to our company. This 'Business Letter' requested our company to make a concession by reducing the real estate price by RMB 7.5 million... Our company hereby informs your company of the relevant matters by this letter: 1. Our company once again urges your company to negotiate with our company on the material matters related to the sale and purchase of this real estate in accordance with the principles of intent reached in the agreement between the two parties, and to sign a formal real estate sale contract. 2. Your company has used our company's business premises for nearly three years. Our company hopes that our two parties, in a practical and realistic manner, can negotiate to determine and finalize the matter of the usage fees payable for your company's use of our company's business premises as soon as possible." Xunjie Company replied in a letter on September 29, 2009, stating: "We have received your letter. Our company takes this matter very seriously. However, as the National Day holiday is approaching, we are busy preparing for the National Day work. We sincerely request your company to postpone the negotiation of the purchase of the first floor of Shudu Building until around October 9. We appreciate your understanding!"

(4) On November 4, 2009, the letter sent by Shudu Industrial Company to Xunjie Company stated: "In order to sign the real estate sale contract, our two parties respectively conducted negotiations on the contents of the real estate sale contract on October 20, 2009, and October 28, 2009. Although full consultations were held, our two parties still had significant differences on the contents of the contract and failed to reach a consensus. Therefore, our company's opinion is: 1. Your company should pay the site usage fees during the period of possession and use of the real estate, and the specific standards can be further negotiated between the two parties; 2. All taxes and fees for the real estate sale shall be borne by your company; 3. Other issues can be discussed again." On November 5, 2009, Xunjie Company replied, stating: "Our company negotiated the purchase of the commercial properties on the north first floor and atrium of Shudu Building with a building area of 2,100 square meters three years ago... However, your company now suddenly raises the issue of site usage fees, and demands that all taxes and fees for the real estate sale be borne by our company. Our company believes that these requirements are too harsh and violate the principle of good faith. We hereby reply clearly as follows: 1. The site usage fee is an additional requirement raised after the establishment of the sale relationship, and our company cannot accept it. 2. The issue of taxes and fees for the real estate sale shall be borne by your company and our company respectively in accordance with national laws, regulations, and government policies. 3. For the remaining purchase price, our company has already prepared dedicated funds. We once again request your company to complete the transfer of the corresponding property right procedures and land procedures to our company's name as soon as possible, after which our company will immediately pay the full amount. The above is our company's written reply to the issues raised by your company. We hope your company can correctly treat the already established sale relationship between the two parties on a practical and realistic basis."

(5) On May 12, 2010, Xunjie Company filed this lawsuit, with the following claims: 1. Request that the court confirm that the letter of rescission issued by Shudu Industrial Company to terminate the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" signed by the two parties on September 20, 2006, is invalid. 2. Request that the court order Shudu Industrial Company to continue performing the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" and perform the obligation of registering the transfer of the real estate ownership. On November 11, 2010, the "Application for Adding Claims" submitted by Xunjie Company to the first instance court stated: "After the people's court provided clarification to the parties, one claim is added. All claims are now listed as follows: 1. Request confirmation that the 'Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate' constitutes a real estate sale contract that has been established and is legally valid; 2. Request that within 15 days after the effective date of the judgment in this case, Shudu Industrial Company perform the obligation of handling the transfer of the real estate to Xunjie Company; 3. Request that within 5 days after the transfer of the disputed real estate, Xunjie Company pay the remaining purchase price of RMB 57.5 million to Shudu Industrial Company; 4. Request that the taxes and fees incurred during the process of transferring the real estate ownership be borne by each party according to legal provisions. The above are the additional claims of Xunjie Company."

The other facts found by the second instance court were the same as those found by the first instance court.

Upon review, the second instance court held that: (1) Regarding whether Xunjie Company had delivered the deposit of RMB 10 million. Although Xunjie Company did not provide direct evidence of paying the RMB 10 million deposit to Shudu Industrial Company, combined with the undisputed facts of the parties, namely: from September 14, 2006, to September 20, 2006, Xunjie Company transferred a total of RMB 10 million to the account of Shuka Fiber Company, a shareholder of Shudu Industrial Company, on several occasions, with the purpose of payment being the advance payment of the real estate purchase deposit. Shuka Fiber Company issued two receipts for the deposit, each in the amount of RMB 5 million, to Xunjie Company on September 20, 2006. On September 20, 2006, Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company signed the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate," which clearly stated: "From the date of signing this agreement, Party A (referring to Shudu Industrial Company) receives a deposit of RMB 10 million from Party B (referring to Xunjie Company)," indicating that Shudu Industrial Company had confirmed receipt of the deposit when signing the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate." During the proceedings, Shudu Industrial Company had no evidence to prove that, apart from the real estate sale relationship in this case, there were other transaction relationships between Xunjie Company and Shuka Fiber Company, a shareholder of Shudu Industrial Company. Moreover, Shudu Industrial Company did not provide evidence to overturn the fact stated in the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" that Shudu Industrial Company had received the RMB 10 million deposit from Xunjie Company for the purchase of real estate. Therefore, its defense that it had not received the RMB 10 million deposit could not stand, and the first instance judgment's finding that Xunjie Company had delivered the RMB 10 million deposit was not improper.

(2) Regarding whether there was a procedural violation in the first instance. On March 8, 2010, Shudu Industrial Company sent a letter to Xunjie Company to rescind the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate." On May 12, 2010, Xunjie Company filed a lawsuit, and its claims included a request to confirm the invalidity of the rescission letter. On November 11, 2010, the "Application for Adding Claims" submitted by Xunjie Company to the first instance court stated that an additional claim was added to confirm that the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" constituted a real estate sale contract that had been established and was legally valid. This "Application for Adding Claims" did not explicitly abandon the claim regarding the invalidity of the rescission letter. The first instance court tried and rendered a judgment based on the parties' claims, which did not violate statutory procedures. Therefore, Shudu Industrial Company's appeal, claiming that the first instance court's trial of this matter was a procedural violation and that Xunjie Company's request to confirm the invalidity of the rescission letter exceeded the statutory time limit, could not stand, and the second instance court did not support it.

(3) Regarding the nature and validity of the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate." In this case, the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" signed by the two parties stipulated that "Party B purchases the north first floor and atrium of Shudu Building owned by Party A, with a building area of 2,100 square meters, at a total price of RMB 67.5 million (final settlement shall be based on the property ownership certificate issued by the real estate management department)." This "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" clearly stated the names of the parties, the subject matter, and the price. The first instance judgment, based on Article 1 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (II)," found that the real estate sale contract relationship between the parties had been established, which was not improper. During the second instance trial, Shudu Industrial Company submitted four copies of "Real Estate Sale Contracts" signed by Shudu Industrial Company with other buyers during the same period. Both parties had no objection to the authenticity of this evidence, and the second instance court confirmed its authenticity. However, the above evidence could not prove that the nature of the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" was a deposit contract. Moreover, during the proceedings, Shudu Industrial Company did not provide evidence to prove that the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" was invalid. The first instance judgment's finding that the agreement was valid was correct. Shudu Industrial Company's appeal, claiming that the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" was a deposit contract and that no real estate sale legal relationship had been formed between the parties because no formal sale contract was signed, could not stand, and the second instance court did not support it.

(4) Regarding whether the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" should be rescinded. After Shudu Industrial Company delivered the real estate to Xunjie Company for possession and use on January 4, 2007, Xunjie Company sent a letter in June 2009 requesting a price reduction. Subsequently, the two parties conducted a series of consultations on issues such as whether site usage fees should be paid, the burden of taxes and fees during the transfer, the handling of the property ownership certificate and the payment time of the balance, and the removal of the mortgage on the sold real estate. During the second instance trial, Shudu Industrial Company submitted a "Tax Advisory Report." Both parties had no objection to the authenticity of this evidence, and the second instance court confirmed its authenticity. This evidence also corroborated the above facts. The consultations between the parties did not result in an agreement, until March 3, 2010, when Shudu Industrial Company sent a letter requesting the rescission of the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" signed by the two parties. During the litigation, after mediation and out-of-court settlement conducted by the people's court, the parties still could not reach an agreement. According to the terms of the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate," "Party A and Party B shall conduct specific consultations on matters such as the real estate purchase contract and payment methods under the principles of this agreement." The parties had the obligation to negotiate and sign a formal real estate sale contract. As the owner of the disputed real estate, Shudu Industrial Company, having delivered the involved property to Xunjie Company for use for more than five years, had neither reached a formal real estate sale contract nor a lease agreement with Xunjie Company. It had received neither the real estate transfer price nor the rent for the real estate, hindering the realization of its property rights. Under the premise that the parties could not reach a formal real estate sale contract, Shudu Industrial Company had the right, in accordance with Article 39 of the "Property Law of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter referred to as the "Property Law"), which provides that "an owner of real property or movable property shall, in accordance with the law, enjoy the rights to possess, use, benefit from, and dispose of the property," to choose the method of disposal of its property and rescind the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" signed with Xunjie Company.

Shudu Industrial Company issued a rescission letter on March 3, 2010. Xunjie Company filed a lawsuit with the court on May 18, 2010. Therefore, the rescission letter issued by Shudu Industrial Company did not have the legal effect of notifying the rescission of the contract. The first instance judgment's support for Xunjie Company's claim was not improper; however, the first instance judgment found that the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" did not meet the conditions for rescission and accordingly ordered Shudu Industrial Company to deliver the involved property within 90 days after Xunjie Company paid the full purchase price, with each party bearing their respective taxes and fees, which was improper. The second instance court corrects this. After the rescission of the above real estate purchase agreement, Shudu Industrial Company's claim for the return of the involved property complies with Article 97 of the "Contract Law," which provides that "after the rescission of a contract, for the part not yet performed, the performance shall be terminated; for the part already performed, the parties may, according to the circumstances of performance and the nature of the contract, demand restoration to the original state, take other remedial measures, and have the right to claim compensation for losses." Although Shudu Industrial Company claimed immediate vacating of the property when filing the lawsuit, necessary preparation time should be granted to Xunjie Company, and the second instance court discretionarily sets this at 30 days.

As for the deposit of RMB 10 million already paid by Xunjie Company, it may assert its rights separately.

(5) Regarding whether Xunjie Company should pay site usage fees. After the two parties signed the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate," Shudu Industrial Company delivered the disputed property to Xunjie Company for use from January 4, 2007, to the present. However, Shudu Industrial Company had no evidence to prove that the delivery was based on a lease relationship or another compensated legal relationship other than the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate." Therefore, Shudu Industrial Company's claim for Xunjie Company to pay site usage fees based on the rent of similar surrounding commercial properties lacks factual and legal basis. Although Xunjie Company had no objection to the authenticity of the "Price Assessment Report" (Hong Jia Ping (2011) No. 53) submitted by Shudu Industrial Company, because this "Price Assessment Report" is irrelevant to this case, the second instance court does not admit it. The second instance court does not permit Shudu Industrial Company's application during the second instance to appraise the site occupation and usage fees for the disputed property from January 4, 2007, to the date of the actual appraisal. The second instance court does not support Shudu Industrial Company's appeal claim for payment of site usage fees.

In summary, the second instance court, after deliberation by its judicial committee, ruled as follows: 1. Uphold Item 1 of the first instance judgment, i.e., "The 'Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate' signed by Xunjie Company and Shudu Industrial Company on September 20, 2006, is established and valid"; 2. Vacate Items 2, 3, 4, and 5 of the first instance judgment, i.e., "The rescission letter issued by Shudu Industrial Company on March 3, 2010, to rescind the 'Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate' signed with Xunjie Company on September 20, 2006, is invalid; within 90 days after Xunjie Company has fulfilled its obligation to pay the purchase price to Shudu Industrial Company, Shudu Industrial Company shall assist in transferring the property located at No. 20, Shuwa North Third Street, Chengdu, the north first floor and atrium of Shudu Building, covering 2,100 square meters, to Xunjie Company, and the taxes and fees incurred shall be borne by Xunjie Company and Shudu Industrial Company respectively in accordance with relevant regulations; Dismiss Xunjie Company's other claims; Dismiss Shudu Industrial Company's other counterclaims"; 3. Xunjie Company shall, within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, vacate and return to Shudu Industrial Company the property located at No. 20, Shuwa North Third Street, Chengdu, the north first floor and atrium of Shudu Building, covering 2,100 square meters; 4. Dismiss Xunjie Company's other claims in the principal lawsuit; 5. Dismiss Shudu Industrial Company's other counterclaims. The first instance principal lawsuit case acceptance fee was RMB 379,300, and the property preservation fee was RMB 5,000, with Xunjie Company bearing RMB 192,150 and Shudu Industrial Company bearing RMB 192,150; the first instance counterclaim case acceptance fee was RMB 87,172.50, with Xunjie Company bearing RMB 43,586 and Shudu Industrial Company bearing RMB 43,586.50. The second instance case acceptance fee was RMB 466,172.50, with Xunjie Company bearing RMB 233,086 and Shudu Industrial Company bearing RMB 233,086.50.

Xunjie Company, dissatisfied with the second instance judgment, applied to this Court for retrial, stating that the basic facts found in the second instance judgment lacked evidence and the application of the law was erroneous. Pursuant to Articles 200(2) and 200(6) of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," it applied for retrial, requesting: to vacate Items 2, 3, and 4 of the second instance judgment and uphold the first instance judgment. The specific reasons were: 1. The "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" signed by Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company constituted a real estate sale contract relationship, which was established and valid, and had been partially performed, and therefore should continue to be performed. The second instance judgment, while finding the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate" valid, that the rescission letter issued by Shudu Industrial Company on March 3, 2010, did not have the legal effect of notifying the rescission of the contract, and that Shudu Industrial Company did not file a counterclaim requesting rescission of the "Agreement for the Purchase of Real Estate," nevertheless groundlessly vacated the first instance judgment's ruling on the invalidity of the rescission letter and ordered Xunjie Company to vacate the property. The logic between the ruling and the court's findings was confused and clearly lacked factual and legal basis. 2. Shudu Industrial Company did not have the right of rescission. The second instance judgment erroneously applied Article 37 of the "Property Law" in a contract dispute case, holding that Shudu Industrial Company had the right to rescind the contract, which was a clear error in the application of the law.

Shudu Industrial Company argued in its defense: 1. The contract in question was a deposit contract for the purpose of establishing a principal contract, intended to guarantee the conclusion of the principal contract. It was a letter of intent for reservation. The principal contract between the parties was always under negotiation and was not concluded for reasons not attributable to either party. 2. Since the principal real estate sale contract could not be concluded, the purpose of the pre-contract could not be achieved. Shudu Industrial Company issued a rescission letter, and the contract in question was rescinded. 3. Xunjie Company's request for continued performance lacked legal basis, and the contract had no specific content for performance and could not actually be performed. 4. In the situation where the sale relationship between the parties had not yet been determined, Shudu Industrial Company delivered the real estate to Xunjie Company based on the lease relationship agreed upon by both parties. Xunjie Company possessed and used the real estate based on the lease relationship. After the rescission of the contract in question, it should vacate the premises and pay the corresponding site usage fees.

Youli Company argued in its defense: 1. Youli Company and Shudu Industrial Company are both independent legal persons. The independent legal status of each cannot be confused simply because Youli Company is a shareholder of Shudu Industrial Company. 2. Youli Company never collected any purchase deposit entrusted or designated by any company. 3. Youli Company has no legal interest in this case and should not be added as a third party in this case.

Shudu Industrial Company, dissatisfied with the second instance judgment, applied to this Court for retrial, requesting: 1. To vacate the first instance judgment; 2. To vacate Items 1 and 5 of the second instance judgment and uphold Items 2, 3, and 4; 3. To order Xunjie Company to pay Shudu Industrial Company site usage fees of RMB 26.509 million for the possession and use of the property in question (as of the time of filing the lawsuit, June 30, 2010). The specific reasons were the same as its defense arguments above.

Xunjie Company argued in its defense: 1. In this case, the parties clearly expressed their true intention to sell and purchase the property in the contract in question, and both parties had partially performed the main obligations of the contract, forming an actual real estate sale contract relationship. The contract in question was the principal contract for the real estate sale, not a pre-contract. The evidence relied on by Shudu Industrial Company to claim that the parties had a real estate lease legal relationship had obvious defects, and this claim had no factual basis. 2. Since Xunjie Company had dedicated funds available for full payment of the remaining purchase price at any time, the property in this case had been delivered to Xunjie Company for use for many years, and the four boundaries of the property were clear, there was no obstacle to the continued performance of the contract in question. Shudu Industrial Company's request that Xunjie Company bear all transaction taxes and fees and its deliberate exaggeration of the tax amounts were excuses to refuse to perform the contract. 3. Shudu Industrial Company did not have the statutory or contractual right of rescission. As the breaching party, it also had no right to rescind the agreement. Xunjie Company filed a lawsuit within three months after receiving the rescission letter from Shudu Industrial Company. Therefore, the letter issued by Shudu Industrial Company did not have the effect of rescinding the contract in question. 4. Shudu Industrial Company's request for Xunjie Company to pay property usage fees and vacate the property lacked legal basis. 5. The continued performance of the contract in question would help stabilize the existing transaction order and maximize the overall wealth of society.

Youli Company argued in its defense that it had no objection to Shudu Industrial Company's request.

This Court finds upon retrial: The facts found by the first instance and second instance courts in this case, "The Chengdu Real Estate Property Rights Supervision Office issued to Shudu Industrial Company on March 4, 2008, the property ownership certificate for the first floor at No. 20, Shuwa North Third Street, Jinjiang District, Chengdu, with an area of 4,060.40 square meters (certificate number: Cheng Fang Quan Jian Zheng Zi No. 1654684, Qiu Di Hao Quan No. 1223775)," contained a clerical error. The correct date for the issuance of this property ownership certificate by the Chengdu Real Estate Property Rights Supervision Office to Shudu Industrial Company should be March 14, 2008. Both parties acknowledged this.

In the retrial of this case, Xunjie Company provided the following evidence: 1. A deposit slip from Xunjie Company's bank account, intending to prove that Xunjie Company has always wished to continue performing the purchase and sale contract and has the ability to do so, and that there is no obstacle to continued performance. 2. A "Tax Consultation Opinion", intending to prove the taxes and fees on the purchase of the property, that Shudu Industrial Company fabricated a huge amount of taxes and fees to create a dispute, and that the actual tax amount is not as high as Shudu Industrial Company claimed. Shudu Industrial Company challenged the evidence, stating that there is no objection to the authenticity of evidence 1, but the deposit date was June 13, 2013, which is seven years after the property purchase agreement signed by the parties in 2006, and therefore it has no relevance to this case. As for evidence 2, because the appraiser for the tax assessment report did not appear in court for cross-examination, its authenticity is not accepted; moreover, the appraisal process ignored the nature of the land under the contract as allocated land, so its legality and relevance are also not accepted. Youli Company challenged the evidence, stating that it agrees with the opinion of Shudu Industrial Company.

Opinion of the Court: In terms of the time of formation, the two pieces of evidence provided by Xunjie Company were both formed after the conclusion of the second instance trial of this case, and can be identified as new evidence for the retrial. As for evidence 1, both Shudu Industrial Company and Youli Company accepted its authenticity, so this Court should confirm its authenticity. As for evidence 2, Shudu Industrial Company and Youli Company have objections to the authenticity of that expert opinion, and moreover, the expert opinion was prepared unilaterally by a consulting company commissioned by Xunjie Company, and the appraiser did not appear in court for cross-examination, so this Court does not confirm its authenticity.

Shudu Industrial Company submitted the last page of a piece of correspondence exchanged by the parties on May 6, 2008, intending to prove that the relationship between the parties was indeed a lease relationship. In response, Xunjie Company challenged, arguing that first, the evidence was incomplete, being only the last page of a multi-page document; second, this evidence cannot prove that the parties had agreed on a lease relationship previously, but only indicates that Xunjie Company would consider changing the relationship from purchase to lease, provided that Shudu Industrial Company paid liquidated damages and compensation; third, this letter was dated May 6, 2008, while the parties' agreement was signed in 2006; this letter can only show that the parties had negotiations regarding modifying the contract, but no agreement was reached. Youli Company challenged, stating that it accepts the authenticity, legality, and relevance of this evidence.

Opinion of the Court: Although this evidence had objectively existed before the conclusion of the second instance trial of this case, considering that Shudu Industrial Company had objective reasons for not providing this evidence before the conclusion of the second instance trial, and there is no evidence that its failure to provide this evidence was due to intentional conduct or gross negligence, it can be identified as new evidence for the retrial. Since Xunjie Company and Youli Company have no objection to the authenticity of this evidence, its authenticity should be confirmed.

Other facts found by this Court in the retrial are the same as those found by the courts of first instance and second instance.

Opinion of the Court: The issues in dispute in this retrial are: 1. The nature and validity of the legal relationship formed between Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company regarding the property involved in the case; 2. Whether the notice of rescission issued by Shudu Industrial Company had the effect of rescinding the contractual relationship between the parties; 3. Whether Xunjie Company's claim for continued performance should be upheld, and whether Shudu Industrial Company's claim for vacating the property and payment of property usage fees should be upheld.

1. Regarding the nature and validity of the legal relationship formed between Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company regarding the property involved in the case.

Based on the relevant assertions and reasons of the parties in the trial of this retrial, two issues closely related to this focus issue need to be clarified first: First, whether Shudu Industrial Company has received the deposit of RMB 10,000,000 paid by Xunjie Company. Although Xunjie Company did not provide evidence of directly paying the deposit of RMB 10,000,000 to Shudu Industrial Company, from September 14, 2006 to September 20, 2006, Xunjie Company made several transfers totaling RMB 10,000,000 to the account of Youli Company (formerly Shuka Fiber Company), a shareholder of Shudu Industrial Company. On September 20, 2006, Youli Company issued two receipts to Xunjie Company, each for RMB 5,000,000. During the trial of this Court, Youli Company stated that it had no other business dealings with Xunjie Company, and there was no contractual or legal basis for receiving this RMB 10,000,000, but thereafter, apart from providing the two receipts to Xunjie Company, there was no further negotiation between the parties regarding this sum. This Court considers that this situation is clearly inconsistent with ordinary daily life and commercial customs. In fact, when combined with other facts found in this case, it can be seen that on September 20, 2006, Article 2 of the "Property Purchase Agreement" signed by Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company clearly states: "From the date of signing this agreement, Party A (Shudu Industrial Company) has received a deposit of RMB 10,000,000 from Party B (Xunjie Company)", indicating that Shudu Industrial Company had already confirmed receipt of the deposit of RMB 10,000,000 paid by Xunjie Company at the time of signing the "Property Purchase Agreement". On November 5, 2009, Xunjie Company's response letter to Shudu Industrial Company mentioned continuing to pay the "remaining" purchase price, and Shudu Industrial Company did not raise any objection to the phrase "remaining purchase price" in subsequent correspondence. On March 3, 2010, the final sentence of the "Letter" sent by Shudu Industrial Company to Xunjie Company through the Chengdu Shudu Notary Public Office stated: "Please process the refund and payment of deposits, usage fees, and other expenses from Xunjie Company." The above facts are sufficient to corroborate each other, proving that Shudu Industrial Company had received the deposit of RMB 10,000,000 paid by Xunjie Company.
