In summary, Shudu Industrial Company's defense that it did not receive the deposit of RMB 10,000,000 cannot be sustained, and the findings of the courts of first instance and second instance that Xunjie Company had paid the deposit of RMB 10,000,000 are correct.

Second, the nature of Shudu Industrial Company's delivery of the property involved in the case to Xunjie Company. The "Property Purchase Agreement" was signed on September 20, 2006, and Shudu Industrial Company delivered the property involved in the case to Xunjie Company for use on January 4, 2007. During the trial of this Court, Shudu Industrial Company submitted a page from the correspondence materials of May 6, 2008 between the parties as evidence. From the content and page number of this evidence, the complete document should have at least two pages. According to Article 31, Paragraph 2 of the "Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings", excerpts from documents and materials shall maintain the completeness of their content and shall not be taken out of context. Therefore, based solely on the content of this single page submitted by Shudu Industrial Company, it is difficult to determine whether the true intention of the parties at the time of delivery of the property was that a lease relationship had already been established, or whether they wished to modify an already determined purchase and sale relationship into a lease relationship. Hence, it cannot prove that Shudu Industrial Company delivered the property based on a lease relationship. Apart from this, Shudu Industrial Company did not provide any other evidence in the first instance, second instance, or retrial to prove that the delivery was based on a lease relationship or other compensated legal relationship outside the "Property Purchase Agreement". Therefore, Shudu Industrial Company has no sufficient evidence to prove that its delivery of the property involved in the case to Xunjie Company was not based on a purchase and sale relationship but on a lease or other compensated use relationship, so its assertion cannot be sustained. The delivery of the property involved in the case by Shudu Industrial Company to Xunjie Company should be identified as a delivery based on the legal relationship of property purchase and sale between the parties.

On the basis of clarifying the above two issues, this Court considers that a legal relationship of property purchase and sale was established between Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company. The reasons are as follows:

First, considering only the "Property Purchase Agreement", its nature should be a preliminary agreement. A preliminary agreement is an agreement to conclude a formal contract in the future. Preliminary agreements take various forms; some have very brief terms, merely expressing the intention to conclude a formal contract in the future, leaving the content of the formal contract to be decided later through negotiation; others have very detailed terms, specifying almost all the content that the formal contract should contain. If viewed solely from the content, the latter is almost identical to a formal contract in terms of the certainty of the contract content, and even if certain terms are missing, they can often be supplemented through contract interpretation. Therefore, the distinction between a preliminary agreement and a formal contract cannot be based solely on the comprehensiveness of the parties' agreement. The fundamental criterion for determining whether a contract signed by the parties is a formal contract or a preliminary agreement should be the expression of intent of the parties, that is, whether the parties intend to conclude a new contract in the future to finally clarify the specific content of the legal relationship formed between them. If the parties have a clear intention to conclude a formal contract in the future, then even if the content of the preliminary agreement is very close to that of the formal contract, and even if the entire content of the formal contract can be derived from the preliminary agreement through contract interpretation, the intention of the parties should be respected, and the possibility of such objective interpretation should be excluded. In this case, the "Property Purchase Agreement" signed by Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company on September 20, 2006 clearly stipulated the location, area, and total price of the property to be bought and sold. It can be said that it contained the main content of a formal property purchase contract and could be directly performed without requiring a separate formal contract. However, the parties also agreed in the same agreement: "...3. Party A and Party B shall conduct specific consultations on issues such as the purchase contract and payment methods under the principles of this agreement. ...5. When Party A and Party B sign the purchase and sale contract for the property, this agreement shall automatically become invalid." It can be seen that although the parties agreed on the location, area, and total price of the property, they still considered that further negotiation on payment methods and other issues was necessary in the future. This expression of intent by the parties is clear, and moreover, Article 5 of the agreement further clarifies the need to sign a new contract in the future to finally determine the specific content of the legal relationship of property purchase and sale between the parties. Therefore, this Court considers that the nature of the "Property Purchase Agreement" is a preliminary agreement. The findings of the courts of first instance and second instance that the "Property Purchase Agreement" is a formal contract are erroneous and should be corrected.

Second, considering the facts of performance by the parties after signing the "Property Purchase Agreement", a legal relationship of property purchase and sale has been established between Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company. This Court considers that whether a relationship between parties constitutes a preliminary agreement or a formal contract cannot be determined solely on the basis of an isolated agreement; rather, it is necessary to comprehensively examine the content of the relevant agreements and the facts of the parties' subsequent negotiations and even specific performance to reach a transaction, seek their true intent, and accurately define the nature of the legal relationship between the parties. In this case, when signing the "Property Purchase Agreement", the buyer, Xunjie Company, had already actually paid a deposit and agreed that it would automatically convert into part of the purchase price under certain conditions, and the seller, Shudu Industrial Company, also accepted the payment from Xunjie Company. More than three months after signing the "Property Purchase Agreement", Shudu Industrial Company delivered the property under the contract to Xunjie Company, and Xunjie Company accepted the delivery. Given the preliminary nature of the "Property Purchase Agreement", the delivery by Shudu Industrial Company should not be regarded as performance of that agreement. In the absence of a lease or other compensated use legal relationship between the parties, the act of Shudu Industrial Company should be identified as a delivery based on the legal relationship of property purchase and sale with Xunjie Company. Accordingly, since the main obligation of Shudu Industrial Company under this legal relationship of property purchase and sale is to deliver the property involved in the case, according to Articles 36 and 37 of the Contract Law of the PRC, it can be determined that the parties reached a consensus on the purchase and sale of the property, and a legal relationship of property purchase and sale was established.

In summary, the legal relationship of property purchase and sale between Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company is established, represents the true intention of the parties, its content does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and is lawful and valid. The courts of first instance and second instance were incorrect in reasoning that the "Property Purchase Agreement" directly constituted a formal contract, but their conclusion that a legal relationship of property purchase and sale existed between Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company is correct.

2. Regarding whether the notice of rescission issued by Shudu Industrial Company had the effect of rescinding the contractual relationship between the parties.

Opinion of the Court: First, according to Articles 93 and 94 of the Contract Law of the PRC, the rescission of a contract includes statutory rescission and contractual rescission. In this case, the parties did not make any agreement on unilateral rescission in the "Property Purchase Agreement" or other related written documents, so Shudu Industrial Company does not have the right of contractual rescission. Under the "Property Purchase Agreement", the main obligations of the parties were to conduct good faith negotiations to reach a consensus on the property purchase and sale, and for Xunjie Company to pay the deposit of RMB 10,000,000. Xunjie Company has paid the deposit of RMB 10,000,000 and has been continuously negotiating with Shudu Industrial Company regarding the property purchase. During the litigation of this case, Xunjie Company also clearly stated that it has the intention and ability to pay the full purchase price. There is no situation of force majeure preventing the realization of the purpose of the contract. Therefore, this case does not meet the statutory conditions for unilateral rescission of the contract. In summary, Shudu Industrial Company's assertion that it has the right to unilaterally rescind the contract cannot be sustained.

Second, according to Article 96 of the Contract Law of the PRC, if a party unilaterally rescinds the contract, it shall notify the other party. The contract is rescinded when the notice reaches the other party. If the other party objects, it may request a people's court or arbitration institution to confirm the validity of the rescission. According to Article 24 of the Judicial Interpretation II of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law, if there is an agreement between the parties on the period for objecting to rescission, that agreement shall prevail; if there is no agreement, the period is three months from the date the notice of rescission reaches the other party. In this case, the parties did not make any agreement on matters including the period for objecting to rescission. Shudu Industrial Company sent a notice of rescission of the "Property Purchase Agreement" to Xunjie Company on March 3, 2010, and the notice reached Xunjie Company on March 8, 2010. Xunjie Company filed the lawsuit with the court of first instance on May 12, 2010. Therefore, regardless of whether Shudu Industrial Company had the right to unilaterally rescind the "Property Purchase Agreement", since Xunjie Company objected by filing a lawsuit within three months of receiving the notice of rescission, the notice of rescission from Shudu Industrial Company also did not have the effect of rescinding the contractual relationship between the parties.

3. Regarding whether Xunjie Company's claim for continued performance should be upheld, and whether Shudu Industrial Company's claim for vacating the property and payment of property usage fees should be upheld.

Opinion of the Court: First, in this case, the parties have made clear and specific agreements on the location, area, and price of the property under the contract. Shudu Industrial Company has delivered the property involved in the case to Xunjie Company, and Xunjie Company has paid the deposit of RMB 10,000,000. Although the parties have not reached an agreement on whether Xunjie Company should pay Shudu Industrial Company for the use of the property site and bear all taxes and fees for the property purchase, in the context where the main rights and obligations of the legal relationship of property purchase and sale between the parties have been determined, the above disputes can be remedied through the principles of contract interpretation as provided in Articles 61 and 62 of the Contract Law of the PRC, and thus do not constitute an obstacle to performance in law or in fact. Moreover, as previously discussed, the legal relationship of property purchase and sale between Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company has been established and become effective, and there are no circumstances under Articles 93 and 94 of the Contract Law of the PRC for rescission of the contract. Therefore, Xunjie Company's claim for continued performance should be upheld.

Second, according to the spirit of Article 15 of the Property Law of the PRC, disposition acts are separate from obligational acts. Rescission of a contract is not a method of disposing of property. Whether a contract is rescinded does not affect the transfer of property ownership, but only relates to whether the parties continue to assume the obligations stipulated in the contract. In this case, Shudu Industrial Company indeed still owns the property, but this does not mean that it can arbitrarily rescind the contractual relationship between the parties under circumstances that do not comply with the parties' agreement or the provisions of the law. After the legal relationship of property purchase and sale is established and becomes effective, although Shudu Industrial Company is the owner of the property, it should fully and actually perform its obligations under the legal relationship of property purchase and sale according to the contract. The judgment of the second instance held that before the subject matter of the sale is transferred, the owner has the right to possess, use, benefit from, and dispose of his subject matter, and thus concluded that Shudu Industrial Company had the right to choose the method of disposing of the property to rescind the contract, and ordered Xunjie Company to vacate the property and return it to Shudu Industrial Company. This contravenes the basic principle of the Contract Law of the PRC to ensure transaction security and represents a misunderstanding and misapplication of the Property Law of the PRC. This Court hereby corrects this.

Third, Shudu Industrial Company's claim for site usage fees from Xunjie Company must have a corresponding legal basis. As previously discussed, the legal relationship between the parties in this case is one of property purchase and sale, not a lease or other compensated use relationship. Shudu Industrial Company's delivery of the property involved in the case to Xunjie Company was based on the legal relationship of property purchase and sale. Therefore, Shudu Industrial Company's claim for site usage fees from Xunjie Company has no factual or legal basis. The findings and rulings of the courts of first instance and second instance on this issue are correct.

In summary, this Court considers that in this case, a legal relationship of property purchase and sale exists between Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company. The parties should perform their respective obligations in good faith. If disputes arise between the parties regarding whether the other party's performance constitutes a breach and whether liability for breach should be borne, they may resolve the matter through negotiation or seek legal recourse separately.

In conclusion, the judgment of the second instance, which held that Shudu Industrial Company had the right to choose the method of disposing of the property to rescind the contract pursuant to Article 39 of the Property Law of the PRC and accordingly ordered Xunjie Company to vacate the property and return it to Shudu Industrial Company, constitutes an error in the application of law. Although the reasoning of the judgment of the first instance that the "Property Purchase Agreement" directly constituted a formal contract is not tenable, its ruling was based on the fact that a legal relationship of property purchase and sale was established and became effective between Shudu Industrial Company and Xunjie Company. This ruling has a legal and factual basis, is relatively appropriate and reasonable, and may be affirmed. In accordance with Article 207 and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. The civil judgment (2012) Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 331 of the Sichuan High People's Court is hereby set aside.

2. The civil judgment (2011) Cheng Min Chu Zi No. 936 of the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court, Sichuan Province, is hereby affirmed.

The allocation of the court costs of first instance and the property preservation fees shall be executed in accordance with the judgment of first instance. The court costs of second instance, amounting to RMB 466,172.50, shall be borne by Sichuan Shudu Industrial Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
